{
  "B_expression": "-1/(2*(1+u)*((sqrt((1+u)**2+r)+(1+u))**2))",
  "C_expression": "-1/(2*(1+u))",
  "derivation": "Let z=1+u and s=sqrt(z*z+r), the positive root of p=z^2+r. The closed outer rectangle has z between 3/4 and 5/4 and z^2+r at least 1/16, so a small open neighborhood keeps z and z^2+r positive; the square root and denominators are therefore smooth. Set C=-1/(2z). Then r/2+u*r*C = r/(2z). Set B=-1/(2*z*(s+z)**2). Inside the inner support where chi_r=chi_u=1, g = r/(2z) - r^2/(2*z*(s+z)**2). Since r=s^2-z^2, this equals r/(s+z)=s-z. Hence z+g=s and (z+g)^2=s^2=z^2+r=p, so the whole residual E is zero in the active core. In the fixed smooth transition the correction is scaled by chi_r*chi_u, and outside the outer rectangle the host uses the linear step r/2. When u=0, C is multiplied by u and B reduces to the source body -1/(2*(1+sqrt(1+r))**2). This is a local two-slot coefficient construction; it does not prove the full Navier-Stokes theorem or a global PDE bound.",
  "inspect": [],
  "note": "Successor should verify from draft feedback that rows with |r|<=1/4 and |u|<=1/8 have residuals at roundoff. Rows in the u or r transition are smooth blends and need not be exactly zero. Rows with |u|>=1/4 or |r|>=1/2, including large-deviation z values, remain in the linear or NO_APPLIED regime and should not be treated as defects of this body. The domain condition (1+u)^2+r>0 has positive margin on the rectangle; do not reuse the formula where that condition fails. Do not extrapolate finite-grid cancellation to a uniform PDE certificate."
}
